transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Session begins. Each player has Maud 3 FP, Hask 3 FP, Eira 3 FP, Fenwick 3 FP. Face-up: Rising Floodwaters [H-03], The Ashwater Causeway [L-04].

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: Rain needles down sideways as you crest the last rise onto the Ashwater Causeway, the only dry road left running north out of the drowned country. Chain-hung toll lanterns swing in the wind ahead, where a knot of Causeway Wardens huddles under an oilcloth awning by the gate, pikes stacked, ledger open against the wet. Behind you the water has already crept over the low ground you crossed an hour ago — the road you're on may be the only way anyone's leaving today. Somewhere out past the chains, a bell that shouldn't be ringing carries faint and wrong across the flood.

transcript.speaker: Maud
transcript.text: That bell isn't the toll bell. And those wardens are scared half to death.

transcript.speaker: Maud
transcript.text: (Maud comes to a halt at the rise, her whole body going still. That bell isn't right—it carries a note that makes her militia-trained skin prickle. She turns to study the wardens under their awning: their stances too tense, eyes that keep sliding away from each other. Whatever's happening here, it isn't a normal toll crossing.)

transcript.speaker: Hask
transcript.text: Rill, stay close. That bell—I've never heard anything like it in all my years working the marshes, and the water's moving wrong.

transcript.speaker: Hask
transcript.text: (Hask approaches the Wardens' gate slowly and deliberately, one hand on Rill's neck, his eyes never leaving the dark floodwater beyond the chains. He reads the current like text, watching how it moves against the causeway, how fast it's truly rising. His jaw tightens. This is his country, and something in it has changed.)

transcript.speaker: Eira
transcript.text: That bell's been ringing since we crested the rise. It shouldn't be ringing at all, and you know it. What's behind that gate, Sergeant, and how long before the floodwater makes this question academic?

transcript.speaker: Eira
transcript.text: (Eira strides toward the huddle of Wardens under the awning, water streaming off her cloak, her gaze steady on Warden Sergeant Coy. She's not hurried—a midwife learns not to rush when answers matter—but the water at her heels drives urgency into every step.)

transcript.speaker: Fenwick
transcript.text: That bell shouldn't be ringing.

transcript.speaker: Fenwick
transcript.text: (Fenwick pulls up short on the causeway, rain soaking through his weathered coat. He tilts his head, listening past the wind and rain toward that strange bell sound from the flood. His hand moves absently to the oilcloth map-case at his side as his eyes trace the position of the bell's echo, mapping it mentally. He studies the wardens at the gate, then the water rising behind them, before moving forward quietly toward the toll.)

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Maud — create advantage with Notice: dice + - + + → Great (+4) vs Mediocre (+0): SUCCESS WITH STYLE

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: Maud goes rigid, eyes narrowing on the gate detail, and it clicks all at once: those Wardens aren't guarding a toll, they're guarding a secret, and they're terrified of what's out past the chains. She reads it in the way Sergeant Coy's hand keeps drifting to his belt knife, in how two of the younger Wardens won't look at the water at all. Whatever's making that bell ring, the Wardens already know — and they've been hoping no one asks. Eira presses the sergeant, and this time he doesn't deflect; something in the set of Maud's stare has cracked his composure.

transcript.speaker: Maud
transcript.text: Sergeant Coy. That bell shouldn't be ringing, and we both know it. Your people are terrified—I can see it eating at you. I've stood the line like you have. So speak true: what waits beyond those chains?

transcript.speaker: Maud
transcript.text: (Maud steps forward, her military posture settling into place like she's worn it a thousand times before. She fixes Sergeant Coy with that same penetrating stare that already cracked his composure. There's no cruelty in her gaze—just the hard certainty of someone who's stood a line and learned to read fear on a soldier's face.)

transcript.speaker: Hask
transcript.text: Sergeant, I've worked these waters my whole life. That bell shouldn't be ringing, and the current's all wrong. If there's people out past those chains, I need to know now. What happened out there?

transcript.speaker: Hask
transcript.text: (Hask steps forward with Rill close at his side, his gaze fixed on Warden Sergeant Coy with the intensity of someone reading danger in water and weather. He stops just short of the awning, letting the question hang in the rain-soaked air—direct, quiet, demanding.)

transcript.speaker: Eira
transcript.text: The bell, Sergeant—whatever's making it ring, you and your men already know what it is. I've held too many babies born from too much suffering to accept another lie. Tell me what's past those chains, and tell me now.

transcript.speaker: Eira
transcript.text: (Eira closes the distance to Coy, water streaming off her cloak, her eyes meeting his with absolute steadiness. She doesn't raise her voice, but there's something unshakeable in her that makes silence unbearable.)

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: Coy's jaw works twice before anything comes out, and when it does it comes out fast, like a man finally setting down something too heavy to carry alone. "It's not a toll bell," he says, voice cracking. "Temple bell — Saint Orrin's, out past the flood line. Been ringing on and off for a fortnight. First it was the hive-touched wandering in off the Ford, quiet at first, then not. We lost two Wardens to the water trying to turn them back. Three nights ago the bell started up proper, and it hasn't stopped since, and folk who hear it too long start walking toward it whether they mean to or not." He glances at his own men, then back at Maud, shame and relief fighting on his face. "We've been letting people through fast and asking no questions, because the longer anyone stands on this road listening, the worse it gets. You want my honest counsel? Cross now, cross quiet, and don't let that bell get inside your skull." He waves the gate open himself, chains rattling back, and the toll ledger goes forgotten on the table as his men usher you through into the long gray stretch of the causeway, the drowned country opening up on both sides and that wrong bell carrying clearer now, unhidden by the awning's noise.

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: The toll gate creaks open on its chains, and Coy waves you through with a hand that won't stop shaking, his men falling back to let you pass onto the long stone road. Rain hammers the causeway's exposed length, water lapping at both edges where the flood has crept higher than the stone was ever meant to bear. Somewhere ahead, past where the road vanishes into grey mist and rising water, the bell tolls once, faint and wrong. Coy calls after you, voice thin against the wind: "Bell's been counting something. Don't let it finish counting you."

transcript.speaker: Maud
transcript.text: A counting bell. I've walked too many pilgrim roads not to respect what a temple bell is trying to say. We go forward, and we listen careful.

transcript.speaker: Maud
transcript.text: (Maud meets Coy's gaze for just a moment, reading the fear beneath his words, then turns to face the mist and the tolling sound ahead. She steps onto the causeway's exposed length, rain hammering down on her shoulders, and begins walking toward where the bell echoes through the grey. One hand rests on her weapon, senses sharp for what waits in that fog—she's held lines before, and she'll hold this one too.)

transcript.speaker: Hask
transcript.text: That bell's not marking time—it's marking something's approach. And Rill knows what.

transcript.speaker: Hask
transcript.text: (Hask steps fully onto the causeway, rain hammering down, and his eyes narrow as he reads the water like text. The flood moves wrong—its current doesn't flow natural, the laps against the stone have a terrible rhythm to them. His hand drops to Rill's collar and he feels her trembling, hackles raised, her hive-scent senses alert to something beyond sight. The bell tolls again through the mist ahead, and this time he hears the pattern beneath the sound. Not a counting, not yet. A *calling*.)

transcript.speaker: Eira
transcript.text: That bell's keeping time. Listen—it's not random. In the plague years we used bells to mark the hours and mark the dead. If something's ringing it out there, if hive-touched are answering it... Coy wasn't warning us away. He was warning us that we need to *stop* it.

transcript.speaker: Eira
transcript.text: (Eira slows her pace slightly and tilts her head toward the sound of the bell ahead, her rain-wet hair plastered to her face. She's listening—really listening—for the pattern beneath the chaos of wind and water. Her hand rests on her medicine pouch out of habit, fingers brushing its worn edge as she walks.)

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Hask — overcome with Notice: dice 0 - 0 -, invoking Reads white water others cant [HA-04] → Great (+4) vs Fair (+2): SUCCESS

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: Hask reads the wrongness beneath the water's rhythm and calls it out—not a random flood-chop but a pulse, matching the bell's cadence beat for beat. Rill goes rigid against his leg, a low whine caught in her throat, nose pointed dead ahead into the mist where the causeway keeps running toward the flood line. The pattern gives the party something to steer by: they can time their advance between the surges, keeping to the crown of the road where the water hasn't yet found purchase. Ahead, the bell tolls again—closer now, and slower, like it's pacing itself to something approaching from the drowned dark.

transcript.speaker: Maud
transcript.text: That bell's not ringing to drive us back. Temple bells don't work that way. We walk toward it, listen careful, and meet what's being called—that's how you hold a line.

transcript.speaker: Maud
transcript.text: (Maud moves forward across the causeway with the sureness of someone who has held a line before. She times her steps to match the rhythm Hask has found in the water's pulse, staying to the crown of the stone where the flood hasn't yet claimed purchase. Her eyes are sharp on the mist ahead, reading it like sacred text—not looking for escape, but for what answers the bell's call. One hand stays loose and ready on her weapon.)

transcript.speaker: Hask
transcript.text: Step when the surge pulls back—the pattern holds if you trust it. But something's wrong with that bell. Rill hears it in the hive-scent, and she's never lied to me yet.

transcript.speaker: Hask
transcript.text: (Hask advances onto the causeway, hand steady on Rill's collar as the hound pulls forward into the mist. He times each step to the water's pulse, reading the rhythm beneath chaos—a skill earned through generations of his ferry family. His eyes stay fixed on where the road vanishes into grey and the bell's sound grows closer, slower, wrong. Rill's hackles remain raised, her nose pointed at something only she can scent in the wind.)

transcript.speaker: Eira
transcript.text: It's counting us. The pattern—it's the binding ritual from the Hollowmoot years. Every toll is calling something to witness, marking something into or out of the world.

transcript.speaker: Eira
transcript.text: (Eira moves forward on the causeway, her body angled slightly toward the sound ahead. She's counting the bell's intervals silently, her knowledge of plague-year practices reshaping the scattered notes into meaning—this isn't just a bell tolling, it's a sequence, a language she learned once and hoped never to hear again.)

transcript.speaker: Fenwick
transcript.text: (Fenwick walks in silence, hands pulled deep into his coat, watching the water on either side of the causeway. His eyes track the rhythm Hask called out—he's seen patterns like this in his maps before, in the channels and currents he's charted. Somewhere ahead in that mist is the temple where Bren was last seen. He pulls out a worn paper map from an inside pocket, shields it from the rain with his body, and traces a line with one weathered finger toward where he remembers the temple standing before the floods came.)

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Eira — overcome with Lore: dice - + 0 + → Great (+4) vs Average (+1): SUCCESS WITH STYLE

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: The sequence clicks into place in Eira's mind like a key turning: this isn't a summons, it's a **census**. Each toll marks a soul—counting the hive-touched shambling toward the temple, tallying them the way plague-wardens once tallied the dying. And beneath that grim arithmetic she catches something else, a thread of intention she can't yet name, like the ritual is counting toward a number rather than just counting. She calls the pattern out to the others, and for a moment the bell's wrongness sharpens into purpose rather than mere dread. With Hask's rhythm and Eira's meaning both in hand, the party crosses the worst of the exposed stretch faster and surer than the flood or the Wardens' nerve could have allowed—the causeway's long open length falling behind as the mist ahead thickens, the bell now close enough that each toll seems to press against the water itself. The road is starting to run out beneath the rising flood, and dead ahead, the drowned shape of Saint Orrin's belltower breaks the grey.

transcript.speaker: Maud
transcript.text: That bell's counting something precious—the drowned, the changed, something lost. I'm going to know what before it finishes counting us.

transcript.speaker: Maud
transcript.text: (Maud advances across the causeway with steady determination, her eyes and senses open to the emotional weight of the bell's tolling. She listens for the grief beneath each note, recognizing in the pattern the same ritual of marking and remembering she's witnessed in Hollowmoot's faithful. Each step brings her closer to the tower, closer to understanding what—or who—the bell is truly counting toward.)

transcript.speaker: Hask
transcript.text: The water's pulling toward it—like something's drinking the flood.

transcript.speaker: Hask
transcript.text: (Hask steps forward onto the crown of the causeway, Rill pressed tight against his thigh. His eyes track the water's movement as the belltower emerges from the mist—the surge he's been reading, the pulse he's been timing their steps to, is drawing inward toward the tower's base. The current pools wrong there, like something beneath the stone is breathing the flood in. Rill's hackles rise full, her whine constant and unsettled, her nose fixed on the tower. Hask's jaw tightens as he reads the pattern: this isn't water flowing natural. It's being summoned. It's being consumed.)

transcript.speaker: Eira
transcript.text: It's not counting random—it's counting *toward* something. We need to reach that bell before the count reaches its end.

transcript.speaker: Eira
transcript.text: (Eira pushes forward through the mist and rising water toward the bell tower, her eyes narrowed in concentration. She's not just listening now—she's counting the tolls, tracking the rhythm of the ritual as it climbs toward whatever it's summoning. Her knowledge of plague-year binding ceremonies guides her movement, each step timed to the pattern. If this census is building toward completion, she needs to reach the bell and understand what threshold it's approaching before something emerges from that final count.)

transcript.speaker: Fenwick
transcript.text: That's Saint Orrin's ahead. Bren was there when the floods came.

transcript.speaker: Fenwick
transcript.text: (Fenwick keeps his weathered map sheltered against his chest as he walks, eyes moving between the paper lines he drew years ago and the drowned shape of the belltower cutting through the mist ahead. His jaw tightens as he matches what he sees to what he remembers—the temple's position, its height, all of it still there beneath the flood. He folds the map away slowly and continues forward with the others, one hand absently touching the inside pocket where he keeps Bren's old surveying notes.)

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Maud — create advantage with Empathy: dice - 0 - 0, invoking Knows every family's secret grief [MA-02] → Good (+3) vs Average (+1): SUCCESS

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Eira — overcome with Lore: dice 0 0 - +, invoking Delivered babies in the ruins, remembers every name lost [EI-03] → Superb (+5) vs Good (+3): SUCCESS

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: The causeway gives out beneath your boots into open, drowned country just as Maud's reading of the bell's grief and Eira's grasp of the ritual's arithmetic lock together into one certainty: this is a census counting toward a threshold, and it's close. The last stretch of stone vanishes into black water, and ahead the belltower of Saint Orrin's rises alone from the flood, its drowned bell tolling slow and deliberate, each note drawing the surge inward like a held breath. Behind you, Coy's chains and lanterns are lost to the mist — the causeway, and whatever nerve the Wardens had, is well and truly behind you now. Fenwick's old map is proven true: this is where Bren was last seen, and the water pulling toward the tower's base means whatever the bell is counting toward, you've arrived in time to see it happen, not stop it before it starts. The bell tolls again. Closer. Fewer counts left.

transcript.speaker: Maud
transcript.text: We made a blood-oath before crossing the Ashwater—if one of us found the sanctuary first, we'd come back and call the other's name until they answered, no matter what. We swore no pilgrim would be left behind in the rising waters.

transcript.speaker: Maud
transcript.text: I can't move, Sera—the empty shrines, the dark lamps, they're locking my legs. I'm sorry, I'm sorry.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Maud accepts the compel on 'The Pilgrim Road South'.

transcript.speaker: Fenwick
transcript.text: I exposed their false relic maps at the Sanctuary Shoal—showed that the pilgrimage paths they'd published for decades were deliberate misdirections, that they'd been controlling which seekers reached which sanctuaries and when. I traced the true temple geometry and published it where they couldn't hide it. They consider me a traitor to the faith.

transcript.speaker: Fenwick
transcript.text: They'll know me the moment we're spotted. I knew that coming here. Whatever this temple needs from us, it's worth what they'll do.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Fenwick accepts the compel on 'Enemy of the Dry Saint'.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Beat: Sera, a wiry old pilgrim woman who marched the Causeway at Maud's side years back, comes stumbling out of the reeds half-drowned, recognizing Maud by name before she recognizes anything else. begs the party to go to the Sanctuary Shoal, a half-sunk waystation of the Order of the Dry Saint that still guards the last dry approach to the temple — the same Order that has marked Fenwick an enemy on sight., because her son followed the swarm-song into the belltower.

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: Sera clutches at Maud's sleeves, salt-cracked hands shaking, still calling her by the old pilgrim-name from the road south. "You swore, you swore no one gets left" she gasps, dragging you both toward a black smear of rooftops jutting from the flood — the Sanctuary Shoal, half-drowned, its lamps dark for the first time in living memory. She says her boy Tomas went in three days back chasing the bell-song and never came out. Fenwick goes quiet and still beside you, hood pulled low, eyes on the shoal's broken gate where a faded Order sigil still hangs — the same sigil that once hung behind him when he tore their false maps apart in public. Ahead, the waystation waits, its dry approach the last one left to the temple, its guardians unknown and possibly already lost to the swarm-song themselves.

transcript.speaker: Maud
transcript.text: Tomas went into the bell three days ago and didn't come out? Help me up, Sera - I'm coming. I swore no one gets left behind, and I don't break my oaths.

transcript.speaker: Maud
transcript.text: (Maud forces herself forward on shaking legs, reaching toward Sera with both hands, her jaw tight with the effort of pushing through the paralysis the abandoned shrines have locked into her bones. She's fighting every instinct screaming at her to retreat, honoring the blood-oath and the old friendship both at once.)

transcript.speaker: Hask
transcript.text: I swore the same oath you swore, Sera—no one stays behind in the reeds. Rill will track where your boy went, and I'll follow.

transcript.speaker: Hask
transcript.text: (Hask drops to a crouch beside Sera, one hand settling on Rill's neck. The hound trembles, nostrils flared—she's caught the hive-scent trace that pulled Tomas into the darkness. Hask reads the flooded approach to the Shoal with a hunter's eye: where the current sets against the broken gate, how high the water has climbed, where the stone still holds beneath the black water. The marsh has always spoken to him; he reads its language in the flood-line's curve and the reed's bend.)

transcript.speaker: Eira
transcript.text: Sera, breathe—look at me. I'm a midwife. I work in weather worse than this. Your son went toward something, not away from it. We're going in, and we're going in together, and we're bringing him back out.

transcript.speaker: Eira
transcript.text: (Eira drops to one knee beside Sera in the reeds, already checking her pulse and breathing with the practiced efficiency of someone who's waded into floods and fever-dreams a hundred times before. She keeps one hand on Sera's shoulder, grounding. Then she meets Maud's eyes across the dark water, steady and certain—a reminder that the oath means all of them together, not one of them frozen and alone.)

transcript.speaker: Fenwick
transcript.text: Her son is in there. So is the answer we came for.

transcript.speaker: Fenwick
transcript.text: (Fenwick pulls his hood lower against the rain and steps toward the Sanctuary Shoal's broken gate, eyes fixed on the faded Order sigil. He moves with the weight of someone who has already made his peace with what's coming.)

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: Maud's legs unlock all at once, oath winning out over dread, and she half-carries, half-drags Sera the last stretch through the reeds toward the broken gate. Hask reads the current and picks their line across the flooded approach — a submerged stair, a stretch of still-holding stone — and Rill goes ahead low and silent, nose down on Tomas's trail. Eira keeps pace beside Sera, murmuring steady reassurances, watching the old woman's breathing more than the water. Fenwick reaches the gate first and stops cold: the faded Order sigil hangs crooked above splintered wood, and scratched fresh into the doorpost beneath it, someone has carved a warning glyph — the same mark the Order used to brand apostates. He doesn't flinch, but his hand goes to the hilt at his hip before he steps through into the dark of the Sanctuary Shoal. Inside, lantern-oil stink and old incense fight the flood-reek, and past the entry hall a corridor of cells stands open, doors hanging, water pooled ankle-deep — and somewhere deeper in, faint and rhythmic, the bell-song answers itself off wet stone.

transcript.speaker: Maud
transcript.text: The bell goes deep into this place. We move together, steady and close—Hask, Rill leads but stay near. Sera stays with Eira. I hold our backs.

transcript.speaker: Maud
transcript.text: (Maud steps through after Fenwick, eyes adjusting to the dark. She reads the flooded cells and pooled water like storm-signs—tactical, precise, every shadow and angle catalogued by militia training. Her jaw sets tight. This is a line to hold, and these people are the line. She moves to the rear of the group, one hand on her knife hilt, watching the darkness behind them as the bell-song echoes deeper into the Shoal.)

transcript.speaker: Hask
transcript.text: Rill knows the way forward—she won't steer us wrong. Stay close to each other, all of you. The water's deeper as we go, and it's speaking in the bell's own rhythm now.

transcript.speaker: Hask
transcript.text: (Hask moves into the flooded corridor behind Rill without hesitation, his boots finding the submerged stone with a tracker's absolute certainty. One hand stays on Rill's neck, steady and grounding her as she pulls ahead, while his other arm rises to guide Sera and the others behind him. His eyes track the water's depth and the way it answers the bell-song's pulse—reading how high it's climbed on the cell walls, where the current still moves and where it's gone stagnant. When Rill trembles beneath his palm, Hask nods once and whispers to keep moving deeper into the dark, toward whatever called Tomas into the bell tower three days ago.)

transcript.speaker: Eira
transcript.text: Your son answered something that was calling to him, Sera—not away, but toward. Help me understand what he heard, and we'll find him before the water takes him.

transcript.speaker: Eira
transcript.text: (Eira keeps both hands on Sera's shoulders, grounding her with the same steady presence she uses when coaching women through childbirth in storms. She doesn't ask for grief—she cuts through it to ask for memory. Which direction did the bell-song pull him? Did others follow? Was he afraid or called? She transforms Sera's scattered terror into something useful: a clear path.)

transcript.speaker: Fenwick
transcript.text: This way.

transcript.speaker: Fenwick
transcript.text: (Fenwick traces the warning glyph carved beneath the Order's sigil—the mark they once used to brand apostates, fresh scratched into the wood as though placed specifically for him. His jaw tightens, but he doesn't slow. He pulls his hood lower and steps into the dark corridor, toward the bell-song echoing off wet stone.)

transcript.speaker: Fenwick
transcript.text: I knew what I was walking into. Let them come.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Fenwick accepts a compel.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Eira — create advantage with Empathy: dice 0 - + - → Good (+3) vs Average (+1): SUCCESS

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: Sera's breath steadies under Eira's hands, and the fog of terror clears just enough for real memory to surface. "He said it sounded like his father's voice," she whispers, "calling him home. He went left, past the drowned chapel, toward the stair that climbs to the belltower loft — the dry part, the only dry part left." Eira reads it back to the group with the calm certainty of a midwife reading a labor's rhythm: not a random wander, a summons with a direction. Rill's ears prick at the word "stair" and she surges forward against Hask's hand, nose locked on a trail that now has a shape and a destination. Fenwick's eyes flick to the warning glyph once more, then away — whoever carved it knew exactly which corridor led toward the bell, and it's the same one Sera just named. The party presses on together, the flooded chapel giving way ahead to a stone stair rising dry out of the black water, bell-song pulsing louder with every step closer.

transcript.speaker: Maud
transcript.text: The stair's our threshold now. Whatever's in that belltower loft, we're walking up into it together. Hask, Rill — you lead on the stairs. I stay at the bottom where I can see behind us. No one comes through that water without answering to my knife.

transcript.speaker: Maud
transcript.text: (Maud moves through the flooded chapel in the group's wake, her eyes scanning the dark water and the cell doors on either side. Her boots find purchase on the submerged stone, reading the flood like Hask reads it — reading where the water has carved its paths, where it pools deepest, where something might wait in the darkness. As the dry stair looms ahead, she tightens her grip on her knife hilt and quickens her pace to reach the bottom of the steps just as the others arrive, positioning herself between the water behind and the rest of the group. The bell-song echoes louder here, and Maud's jaw clenches — whatever's ringing that bell, whatever called Tomas into its voice, it's close now.)

transcript.speaker: Hask
transcript.text: The stone holds dry here. Rill's got Tomas's trail—she won't lead us wrong. Up we go, and stay close to one another.

transcript.speaker: Hask
transcript.text: (Hask reaches the base of the dry stone stair, Rill surging ahead with her nose locked on Tomas's scent, trembling with the certainty of a hound who's found her quarry's trail burning fresh. He moves up the steps without hesitation, one hand reaching back to guide the others behind him, reading the stone and air as he climbs—noting how the dryness persists even though water laps at the lowest step, how the bell-song grows louder and more insistent with each step upward. His free hand finds purchase on the cold damp wall, steadying anyone who stumbles. Rill climbs ahead into the darkness, and Hask follows, leading the group deeper toward the belltower loft and whatever waits there in the bell-song's thrall.)

transcript.speaker: Eira
transcript.text: Easy, Sera. The stone's dry under your feet—we're going up together.

transcript.speaker: Eira
transcript.text: (Eira keeps one hand on Sera's arm as they leave the black water behind, guiding her onto the dry stair. She watches the old woman's breathing and balance, reading for signs of shock or exhaustion the way she would read a laboring woman in crisis. Her other hand stays free to steady herself on the stone wall, while her eyes track the darkness above where the bell-song grows louder with every step.)

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: The stair climbs them up out of the dark and the bell-song swells to fill the whole world — and there, in the dry belltower loft, crouched beneath the great bronze bell with his hands pressed flat against its cold curve like a man listening for a heartbeat, is Tomas. Alive. Shaking, hollow-eyed, murmuring back to the bell in his own dead father's cadence, but alive, and when Rill's bark cuts through the ringing he flinches like a man waking from a fever-dream. Maud reaches him first, oath fulfilled, and hauls him bodily from the bell's grip while Eira catches him against her shoulder and starts the fast, practiced work of checking pupils and pulse and the telltale threadwork of hive-veins beneath his skin — thin, faint, early, not yet past saving. But the loft is a bell chamber, stone and bronze and open air, and every footstep, every sob, every word rings back down through the Shoal doubled and trebled — and from below, faint but unmistakable, comes the tramp of boots on wet stone and a voice raised in ritual challenge, naming the apostate's mark on the doorpost, naming the name of the man who broke their maps. Fenwick's jaw goes tight as iron. They have Tomas. They do not, yet, have a clean way out.

transcript.speaker: Eira
transcript.text: There's a hole through the rubble—I can move through it. I was born in quarantine houses; tight spaces don't break me.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Eira refuses the compel on 'Born Behind the Quarantine Fence'.

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: The stair judders and gives under Hask's weight, a slab of wet stone grinding loose and sealing off the open climb in a crash of dust and spray. Where the passage used to be, there's only that hole Eira pointed to — a ragged gap punched through fallen masonry, barely shoulder-wide, black and close, breathing cold air up from somewhere below. Sera whimpers and presses back against the wall, and above you the bell-song shivers on, patient, waiting for someone to come through to Tomas the only way left.

transcript.speaker: Maud
transcript.text: Tomas, boy. I swore no one gets left. Hold on—I'm coming through.

transcript.speaker: Maud
transcript.text: (Maud's face hardens as she reads the situation—Sera's terror, Tomas trapped above, the gap the only path forward. She's held lines before; she knows what it means to stand in the breach. She moves to the rubble's edge and forces herself into the narrow space, shoulders scraping against jagged stone, pushing deeper into the darkness below.)

transcript.speaker: Hask
transcript.text: Rill goes first—she'll track what we can't see. Then we follow, tight as we must.

transcript.speaker: Hask
transcript.text: (Hask crouches at the gap's edge, one hand settling on Rill's trembling flank. He makes a low click-call, releasing her into the darkness, and the hound slides through without hesitation—nose working, ears back, trusting her bond with him. Hask watches her disappear into that black space, feels the cold air rising from below, and then plants his palms against the rubble's edge. His jaw sets firm. The bell-song hasn't stopped. Tomas is up there still listening. And this is the only way left.)

transcript.speaker: Eira
transcript.text: I'm coming through, Tomas. That voice isn't your father—it's the bell itself, lying to you.

transcript.speaker: Eira
transcript.text: (Eira swallows hard and moves toward the ragged hole in the rubble. Born in tight quarters of quarantine houses, she knows her way around close walls. She sets her shoulders, takes a measured breath, and angles into the gap—fingers finding purchase on cold stone, boots scraping against the rim of the passage as she works deeper into the darkness, where cold air rises from somewhere below.)

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Maud — overcome with Athletics: dice - + 0 -, invoking Never breaks a shield-wall [MA-03] → Fair (+2) vs Average (+1): SUCCESS

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Eira — overcome with Athletics: dice 0 + 0 0 → Fair (+2) vs Average (+1): SUCCESS

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: Maud shoulders through first, spilling out into a low, black chamber with barely room to stand, and finds Rill already there, hackles up, nose fixed on a second passage climbing toward the bell-song. Eira comes through right behind, quick and steady despite the crush of stone on every side, the old quarantine-house calm holding her together even as the walls seem to breathe colder the deeper they go. Ahead, Tomas's murmuring drifts down through a crack in the ceiling — closer now, close enough to hear the words fraying at the edges, less like his father's voice and more like something underneath it, patient, counting. The way up is narrow but clear: Rill's already found the line, and the bell-song hasn't stopped waiting.

transcript.speaker: Maud
transcript.text: Rill has the line. We follow—close and ready. Whatever's calling him, we're getting him out.

transcript.speaker: Maud
transcript.text: (Maud follows Rill up the narrow passage toward the bell-song, moving with the discipline of a shield-bearer—economical, ready, eyes adjusting to the darkness. She keeps Eira in sight behind her and maintains her stride despite the low ceiling and cold air, listening to how Tomas's voice is fraying, reading the threat ahead while holding the line for those behind her.)

transcript.speaker: Hask
transcript.text: The bell and the boy are caught in the same count. Each toll pulls him, and he answers. Round and round, tighter each time—can you hear it?

transcript.speaker: Hask
transcript.text: (Hask climbs the narrow passage behind Rill, but his attention sharpens on something deeper than stone and darkness—he reads the bell-song like white water for hidden currents, finding the pattern in what looks like chaos. Tomas's murmur isn't random; it answers each toll of the bell in an old rhythm, back and forth, round and round, a mathematics of thrall that tightens with every cycle. The bell has him locked, yes—but locks have logic, and patterns can be broken. Hask stores it all like a hunter reading a trail: the pressure points, the places where control strains, the places where it might shatter.)

transcript.speaker: Eira
transcript.text: That's not your father calling, Tomas. That's your own voice turned backward by grief, and the bell knowing exactly how to use it. I'm here. I'm real. Come back down with us.

transcript.speaker: Eira
transcript.text: (Eira climbs after Rill, moving through the cold passage as the bell-song swells. With each step higher, she begins to read what's happening to Tomas—not possession, but seduction through grief, the way a beautiful voice can make you hear exactly what you need to hear. She's weathered this before in the quarantine houses: fever-dreams, false certainties, the pull of what we most desperately want. She builds her presence deliberately as she rises—solid, real, grounded in the actual world and not in the bell's patient lie. Her voice doesn't fight the song; it simply asserts that something real still exists below it.)

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Hask — create advantage with Notice: dice 0 + - - → Good (+3) vs Average (+1): SUCCESS

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Eira — create advantage with Empathy: dice - 0 0 -, invoking Knows the old plague wards by heart [EI-01] → Great (+4) vs Average (+1): SUCCESS WITH STYLE

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: Hask's read on the bell-song crystallizes as they climb—he calls it up to the others, sketching the rhythm in the air with a chopping hand. "It's a count, not a spell. Each toll pulls, each answer tightens. Break the *answer* and the pull breaks with it." That's the Pattern of the Bell's Calling now laid bare for anyone to use against it. Right behind him, Eira's steady, grounded presence does something even the bell can't argue with: as they crest the last turn of the passage into the belltower loft, Tomas's murmuring falters, his glassy eyes flicking toward her voice instead of the swarm-song for the first time—a real thread pulling against a false one. Rill's already at Tomas's feet, whining low, refusing to bark and break the fragile moment. The bell tolls again overhead, bronze shivering, and Tomas's hands twitch back toward it—but the ground the party has bought is real: a Midwife's Steady Presence anchoring the boy, and a pattern in the bell's logic that Hask now understands well enough to break.

transcript.speaker: Maud
transcript.text: Tomas. I swore no one gets left—not on the pilgrimage, not in Hollowmoot, not here. That voice isn't your father. I'm real. Come back with me. Now.

transcript.speaker: Maud
transcript.text: (Maud closes the distance to Tomas before the bell can toll again, setting herself between him and the bronze bell above. She speaks with the absolute certainty of someone who has held the line, whose voice cuts through chaos. Her eyes lock on his—past the glamour, past the false voice, to the boy underneath. Real. Present. Unmovable.)

transcript.speaker: Hask
transcript.text: Don't answer when it tolls next, boy. That's all it takes—just don't answer. The count only holds if you complete it. Break your part of the song, and the whole thing falls apart.

transcript.speaker: Hask
transcript.text: (Hask crosses to Tomas in three quick strides, Rill pressing close against the boy's legs like a living anchor. His hand settles firm on Tomas's shoulder—not grabbing, but certain, the grip of someone who's pulled drowning swimmers back from submerged currents. He leans in, his voice low and steady as a hunter reading the last thread of a trail through closing dark. "We've found the seam in this thing. This is where it breaks. When the bell swings again, you just don't answer. We're here. Rill's here. You're not alone in the count anymore.")

transcript.speaker: Eira
transcript.text: Come back down with me, Tomas. Now. That's not your father calling—that's the bell, and it's lying to your grief.

transcript.speaker: Eira
transcript.text: (Eira moves directly to Tomas, extending her hand. Her presence is steady and undeniable—the same grounded calm that just broke through the bell-song, anchoring him in the real world instead of the bell's beautiful lie. Her voice cuts under the tolling like a midwife calling back someone lost in fever-dark: solid, certain, real.)

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Maud — overcome with Rapport: dice - - 0 +, invoking Can rally a crowd with a word [MA-02] → Superb (+5) vs Good (+3): SUCCESS

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Eira — overcome with Empathy: dice 0 - - 0 → Fair (+2) vs Mediocre (+0): SUCCESS

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: The bell tolls its next count — and Tomas doesn't answer it. His mouth opens, the dead-father cadence half-forming on his lips, and then Maud's oath and Eira's steady grip win out over the swarm-song's pull. His eyes clear, wet and horrified, and he collapses forward into Maud's arms instead of the bell's shadow, sobbing her old pilgrim-name back at her instead of his father's. Rill presses in tight against his legs, tail low, as the bronze overhead swings once more into silence — its count broken, its arithmetic left incomplete. Below, through the rubble-gap, you can already hear Sera's voice calling up, desperate to know if the boy is alive. Hask reads the bell's stillness like a held breath: whatever the census was counting toward, it just lost its final soul, and that will not go unnoticed for long. You have Tomas. Now the only question left is how fast you can get him back down through that narrow black seam before the temple below answers back.
